pr_body:
# What does this PR do?

A recent PR #31238 updated the `is_torch_xpu_available` check to reflect XPU support from Pytorch >= 2.4. However, this broke backwards compatibility with versions of pytorch < 2.4 when `is_ipex_available` is `False` and `check_device=True`. 

Technically, this fails if the installed torch in the environment is <= 2.2, and 2.3 will still pass, as torch 2.3 has the `torch.xpu` module. However, as the intended logic is to default to the pytorch available logic for >= 2.4 and previously this evaluated to False for 2.3, this is more backwards compatible. 

Fixes #31563

issue_context.title: Transformers master version breaks compatibility with `torch<2.3`
issue_context.body:
### System Info

transformers master version: `pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/transformers`
torch version < 2.3, e.g. `pip install "torch==2.2"`
python 3.9
Ubuntu 22.04

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [ ] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

```
from transformers.utils.import_utils import is_torch_xpu_available

is_torch_xpu_available(check_device=True)
```
raises error `AttributeError: module 'torch' has no attribute 'xpu'`

```
>>> from transformers.utils.import_utils import is_torch_xpu_available
>>> is_torch_xpu_available(check_device=True)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "/home/weichen.xu/miniconda3/envs/mlflow/lib/python3.9/site-packages/transformers/utils/import_utils.py", line 765, in is_torch_xpu_available
    _ = torch.xpu.device_count()
  File "/home/weichen.xu/miniconda3/envs/mlflow/lib/python3.9/site-packages/torch/__init__.py", line 1932, in __getattr__
    raise AttributeError(f"module '{__name__}' has no attribute '{name}'")
AttributeError: module 'torch' has no attribute 'xpu'
```

### Expected behavior

No error raised but return `False`
comments:
Hi @WeichenXu123, thanks for reporting! 

I've opened #31573 which should fix this

review_comments:
Previously, if `is_ipex_available` evaluated to `False` we would return `False`. #31238 enables using pytorch for XPU as well, if the installed version >= 2.4. 

Here, we still return `False` if the installed version < 2.4 and IPEX is not available in the environment

Thanks.

Could also be fixed by change `except RuntimeError` to `except RuntimeError, AttributeError`, but both works for me and leave you to make the call.
I'll leave like this, as it makes the intended behaviour a bit more explicit imo :)
